decisions: QueueDeadLetterSink implements the T035 DeadLetterSink contract and uses the T027 QueueSender boundary, so the worker sends a structured envelope before deleting an exhausted source message.

The envelope retains exact original content, source delivery identifiers, attempt count, UTC failure time, full error text, and parsed error type/detail. Its stable ID excludes pop receipt and attempt count so repeated transfer is diagnosable.

DeadLetterReplayer sends the original JSON object to the original queue and requires an explicit repaired mapping for malformed or non-object content. Replay is operator-triggered, one message at a time, and never automatically retries or deletes the dead-letter record.
InMemoryDeadLetterStore provides deterministic lookup, ordering, and stable-ID replacement for focused recovery tests and local tooling without pretending to be durable production storage.
limitations: T027 QueueSender accepts JSON mappings rather than raw queue bytes; malformed or non-object source content requires an operator-approved repaired mapping for replay.
Dead-letter transfer and source deletion remain separate queue operations. A stable ID identifies duplicate transfers, but cannot provide an atomic cross-queue transaction.
No live Azure, provider, credentials, network access, CLEO mutation, staging, revert, commit, or MyPy run was used.
The shared worktree contains unrelated user changes and untracked files; none were modified, staged, reverted, or committed by T063.
